one_line: A satirical desk HR simulation that makes state-gated WebMCP actions visible.
what_it_does: Turns eight desk objects into employees and lets a human and browser agent inspect records, review, promote, relocate, and terminate with state-dependent tools and human approval for irreversible actions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central: typed tools, live state-derived availability, state-built schemas, human-in-the-loop gating, and an audit record are materially safer and more reliable than generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies nine typed document.modelContext tools.
resolve_pip is registered only while a PIP is open; terminate rejects alumni and recently promoted staff.
Irreversible actions pause through requestUserInteraction or return requires_user_action without state change.
Frame sheets show a human-visible desk state, object record, and agent action progression.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, intentionally scoped demo and frame sheets show the running desk, selected records, visible movement, and an Agent action log; exact end-to-end completion is not fully legible and no transcript is supplied.
execution_evidence: Live demo is reported alive.
Three frame sheets show changing desk state and detail panels.
Visible captions and UI indicate successful structured action and audit logging.
No video transcript and small text limit verification of every state gate.
impact_rationale: It is a memorable, concrete reference for teams designing safe agent actions, especially irreversible operations, while remaining easy to understand through satire.
impact_evidence: Targets operational products exposing refunds, deletion, payouts, and approvals to agents.
Demonstrates shared human-agent state and auditable decisions.
Mug/desk metaphor makes the safety contract inspectable quickly.
creativity_rationale: The HR treatment of desk objects is an original, memorable interaction model used deeply enough to explain capability gating and approvals.
creativity_evidence: Eight desk objects become staff with personnel files.
Upper Management versus browser-agent HR framing.
Termination and PIP workflow turns protocol behavior into an accessible simulation.
usability_note: Single-screen visual metaphor and explicit records make the workflow approachable; dense state rules may still require orientation.
advance_reason: Distinctive, well-evidenced WebMCP safety demo with meaningful protocol delta.

one_line: A deterministic factory decision lab shared by a planner and browser agent.
what_it_does: Reads factory state, creates and edits bounded scenarios, simulates shifts, compares receipts, and handles human lock changes with stale-write rejection and infeasibility proof.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP supplies a shared versioned command surface with typed narrow tools, atomic stale-write rejection, live capability changes, and immutable receipts; generic UI driving cannot comparably guarantee this coordination.
leverage_evidence: Six tools share the same command path as the UI and operate on one versioned state.
Human Packaging lock advances revision; old agent write is rejected atomically as STALE_FACTORY.
Capability map changes after lock and supplier phase closure.
Receipt-backed deterministic simulation and comparison are described and shown across replay frames.
execution_rationale: The central workflow is unusually complete and coherent: mission constraints, two scenarios, simulation receipts, human intervention, stale rejection, replanning, and an upper-bound infeasibility result are all evidenced by the packet and replay.
execution_evidence: 177-second video exists with complete WebMCP replay frame sheets.
Transcript reports Scenario A and B at 11,114 units, with B passing cost cap.
Post-lock retry rejects atomically without state mutation.
Fresh replanning produces 9,114 units and proves upper bound 9,252 below target 10,937.
impact_rationale: Factory planners and operations teams have a real coordination and authority problem; this directly demonstrates safer, auditable decision support under changing constraints.
impact_evidence: Concrete production mission with output, cost, machine, and defect constraints.
Addresses handoff loss across dashboards, spreadsheets, specialists, and approvals.
Proves an actionable infeasibility result rather than merely recommending a plan.
creativity_rationale: The combination of live human locks, versioned agent planning, deterministic receipts, and proof of infeasibility is a notably original interaction model for a hackathon.
creativity_evidence: Human and agent replan the same live factory state.
Stale-write rejection is made part of the product experience.
Conservative upper-bound proof answers what cannot be achieved under current authority.
usability_note: Narrow tools and shared decision state support expert planning, though factory concepts and dense evidence may be demanding for new users.
advance_reason: Top-tier leverage and execution with unusually strong evidence and a credible operations use case.

one_line: A patient portal designed for caregivers and their signed-in agents.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP bridges an authenticated portal that lacks an agent API while preserving portal-owned permission tiers, confirmation, and shared navigation state; generic UI driving is less safe and reliable.
leverage_evidence: Agent works across four modules in an already signed-in session.
Reads are available, writes prepare confirmation cards and do not submit until approval.
Consent, full-record access, and proxy-permission changes have no tools.

one_line: A privacy wallet exposing expiring threshold claims instead of raw personal facts.
what_it_does: Stores sensitive facts locally, turns them into narrow claims, and registers only consented, time-limited claim tools so agents cannot request raw values.
leverage_rationale: The tool registry itself is the privacy boundary: capabilities appear and disappear with consent, and raw-value tools never exist. This is a structural delta from UI automation or permissive agent APIs.
leverage_evidence: Claims are generated locally and exposed as narrow predicates.
getTools() no longer lists a capability after consent lapses.
No get_income or get_date_of_birth tool exists at any point.
User chooses claims and duration; live registry proves absence.
execution_rationale: The concept and interface claims are coherent, with three frame sheets and twelve gallery images, but no transcript and no public repository reduce inspectability.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive.
Three frame sheets show wallet/registry states.
About text describes consent, timers, and live registry absence.
Public repository is false and video is absent.
impact_rationale: People completing eligibility forms have a real privacy and data-minimization problem; threshold claims can preserve utility while reducing sensitive disclosure.
impact_evidence: Concrete housing-program eligibility example.
Addresses over-parameterized forms and agent context leakage.
Raw personal values remain browser-local and are never exposed as tools.
creativity_rationale: Treating capability existence as the privacy control, with nonexistence of raw-value tools as a design invariant, is novel and deeply aligned with the medium.
creativity_evidence: Registry disappearance on consent expiry.
Predicate claims replace raw data retrieval.
Explicitly responds to a risk identified in the WebMCP specification.
usability_note: The claim model is understandable and privacy-preserving, though users may need help mapping facts to predicates.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage, impact, and originality; execution evidence is adequate but not maximal.
